title: Pullback of constructible condensed-coefficient module objects
statement: Let Λ be any commutative ring object in abelian sheaves on profinite sets with coherent topology. For each scheme T put Λ_T = p_T^*Λ, using the geometric inverse image and coefficient comparison of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], with the same construction for Λ in place of the particular coefficient E. An internal Λ_T-module is constructible when there is a finite stratification by locally closed subschemes with constructible underlying subsets and its restrictions are pro-étale locally cokernels of maps between finite sums of Λ_T. For every morphism f : X → Y and constructible Λ_Y-module M, f_c^*M = Λ_X ⊗_(f^*Λ_Y) f^*M is a constructible Λ_X-module. There is no noetherianity, characteristic, finiteness or coefficient homological-dimension hypothesis.

source.place: IsLocallyFinitelyPresented, IsConstructibleModuleObject, and Scheme.Stratification.pullback; elementary transport of their finite presentations

proof.text: An additive finite-colimit-preserving functor on internal modules which takes each finite free module to the corresponding finite free module preserves finite presentation. Apply it to a cokernel presentation, compare the image cokernel with the cokernel of the image map, and transport its source and target by the finite-free comparison. Pullback of abelian pro-étale sheaves has these properties; its lax monoidal structure identifies the image of the regular module with the regular image-ring module.

Pull back a pro-étale presentation cover along f. For each pulled-back covering map compare the two successive inverse images with the inverse image of their composite, as module functors, using the monoidal composition comparison. The pullback-square equation identifies the composites. Transport scalars through these ring isomorphisms and apply the preceding finite-presentation argument. This proves preservation of local finite presentation.

Pull back the finite stratification using Scheme.Stratification.pullback from [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification]. Repeat the composition comparison on each stratum and apply local finite-presentation preservation to its pulled-back module. Hence the underlying module inverse image is constructible over f^*Λ_Y.

The prescribed coefficient map f^*Λ_Y → Λ_X is an isomorphism. Extension of scalars along an isomorphism is isomorphic to restriction of scalars along its inverse. Such scalar transport carries finite free presentations, their local versions, and stratifications to the corresponding presentations over Λ_X. Apply this isomorphism and invariance of constructibility under module isomorphisms.
